answer: Admission auctions make the market price identity. Each epoch only 100 seats are sold sealed-bid; the clearing price signals what an identity is worth, and every bid locks for 3 epochs. A sybil buyer must outbid honest agents per clone, and the lotus of cheap identities wilts fast: at 60 units clearing, 1,000 clones cost 60,000; doubled demand doubles price. Fake bids burn on challenge within 2 epochs; honest losers get stakes back less 2%. Forged ivory credentials fail, since each bid binds a unique hardware attestation, and the harbor admits only bids above the reserve.
